[Unit]
Description=0509 search tier canary — daily §1.8 six-domain regression guard (issue #1452)
# Fails (exit non-zero) when any of the six §1.8 domains returns 0
# verified/likely rows on production /search?q=<domain>&country=all.
# Deliberately a user unit on the fleet VPS (like agent-cron-*): the worker
# GitHub App token cannot create or update .github/workflows files, and the
# check needs no secrets — only outbound HTTPS to 0509.io.

[Service]
Type=oneshot
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
ExecStart=/usr/bin/env node scripts/search-tier-canary.mjs
# Evidence: one plain-text run log; the unit's failed state is the loud
# signal (systemctl --user list-units --failed) and the log keeps the
# per-domain tier counts for observe-to-close.
StandardOutput=append:<local-path>
StandardError=inherit
# Six fetches with 429 backoff worst case (~6 x 4 x 60s) must still finish.
TimeoutStartSec=30min
# A failed canary must stay failed for operators; do not restart into a loop.
Restart=no

[Unit]
Description=Daily 08:15 IST — 0509 daily market signal (agent-agnostic)

[Timer]

[Unit]
Description=Agent-agnostic cron: 0509 daily market signal (migrated from hermes 7a46414b01b6)
# Agent-agnostic substrate per agent-agnostic-audit-2026-08-25.md Surface 1.
# Schedule moved from hermes cron; original hermes job is now PAUSED but
# preserved as migration provenance (never deleted).
#
# fleet-ops#143: the ExecStart wrapper (agent-cron-run) now rotates seats via
# pick_seat instead of gating on the single-snapshot lanes/pi-seat-health.json.
# Restart=on-failure re-runs ExecStart, which picks a DIFFERENT seat each
# retry, so a transient fleet 429 in the wrong minute delays the daily job
# instead of killing it for the day. RestartSec=15min + StartLimitBurst=3
# bounds the retry window: three re-seats within the hour, then the unit goes
# to failed until the next timer trigger (tomorrow).
StartLimitIntervalSec=1h
StartLimitBurst=3

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
# issue #2018 (Nishfleet/0509): the seat previously ran in the SHARED product
# checkout, where another agent's unsaved scratch file blocked the whole morning
# report at the clean-checkout gate. The seat now owns a dedicated worktree under
# agent-state, refreshed each run, so no other agent's work can ever block it.
# The seat only ever refreshes its OWN directory — it never touches the shared
# checkout and never moves or deletes any other agent's file. Fail-loud behaviour
# is preserved; see prompts/0509-daily-market-signal.md "Failure semantics".
Environment=WORKDIR=<local-path>
Environment=LOG_DIR=<local-path>
Environment=PROMPTS_DIR=<local-path>
Environment=PI_BIN=<local-path>
# Provision + refresh the seat's dedicated worktree (a standalone clone of the
# public Nishfleet/0509 repo at origin/main). First run clones; later runs
# fetch + reset + clean so the report always runs against current main and never
# into another agent's leftover files. Failures exit non-zero so the existing
# Restart=on-failure seat-rotation retry still applies (fail-loud preserved).
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c 'W=<local-path>; U=https://github.com/Nishfleet/0509.git; if [ -d "$W/.git" ]; then git -C "$W" fetch --quiet --depth 1 origin main || { echo "0509-daily-market-signal pre: fetch failed" >&2; exit 1; }; git -C "$W" reset --hard --quiet origin/main || { echo "0509-daily-market-signal pre: reset failed" >&2; exit 1; }; git -C "$W" clean -fdq || { echo "0509-daily-market-signal pre: clean failed" >&2; exit 1; }; else git clone --quiet --depth 1 "$U" "$W" || { echo "0509-daily-market-signal pre: clone failed" >&2; exit 1; }; fi'
ExecStart=<local-path> 0509-daily-market-signal
# Retry policy — a transient fleet 429 delays the job, not kills it for the
# day. systemd re-runs ExecStart (which re-seats via pick_seat) up to
# StartLimitBurst times within StartLimitIntervalSec.
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=900
# Hang detection: a cron active longer than this is terminated into `failed`.
# (TimeoutStartSec, not RuntimeMaxSec: systemd ignores RuntimeMaxSec on
# Type=oneshot.) agent-cron-run also bounds pi itself (PI_HANG_TIMEOUT_S) to
# 42min, shorter than this, so a wedge clears its seat before this fires.
TimeoutStartSec=45min

[Unit]
Description=Bounded-file maintainer for the escalation channel
Documentation=file:<local-path>

# fleet-ops#2677 + #2773: NISH-ESCALATIONS.md and alert-repair packets
# accumulate indefinitely. This drain keeps the live files bounded by
# archiving RESOLVED / REVOKED / non-class noise out of NISH and deleting
# consumed alert-repair packets. The drain is idempotent and
# best-effort — a failed run is loud (rc=1 climbs the escalation ladder
# via service.d/10-escalate.conf) but never re-fires.
#
# Anti-recursion: this unit inherits service.d/10-escalate.conf. A genuine
# fail-loud exit (jq missing, etc.) climbs the SENIOR-AUDITOR rail. A
# clean run with nothing to do is rc=0 silent.

Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
# ExecStart via `bash -c exec` mirrors escalation-daily-sweep.service — the
# CI unit-verify job stubs VPS binaries and a bare ExecStart=<local-path>
# would fail hosted verification before install.sh deploys the bin.
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path>
TimeoutStartSec=2min
# Fail loud: no Restart=, no SuccessExitStatus fudging. A non-zero exit must
# leave this unit in `systemctl --user list-units --state=failed` so the
# escalation ladder (service.d/10-escalate.conf -> unit-escalation@) climbs
# to the senior auditor.
Restart=no

Description=Fleet orchestrator heartbeat (durable, session-independent, host-local)
# Named reason for this schedule (vault: "a schedule needs a NAMED reason"):
# orchestrator continuity across interactive-session restarts; event
# notifications die with sessions. The previous watcher/cron was session-
# bound and died 4x today on session hops; this timer is owned by the
# user systemd instance, not by any agent or tmux session.
#
# fleet-ops#3270: the three sections that only read GitHub state
# (lifecycle-label-sweep, merged-pr observe-to-close, close-duplicates)
# moved behind webhook triggers (gh-webhook-receiver
# dispatches to their own .service units). tier 1 now keeps only
# host-local sections: merge-to-live deploy, queue green PRs, release
# orphaned claims, recover failed units, verify scout/intake timers,
# update the last-heartbeat stamp, re-examine agent-blocked issues, RAM
# measurement, seat-health freshness, and the canaries. The timer
# cadence dropped 15 -> 60 min because the webhook fast-path covers the
# GitHub-state freshness contract; host-local ops have no upstream event
# signal and 60 min is proportionate.
#
# Two-tier design (P13 amendment, 2026-08-25):
#   tier 1 (deterministic, no LLM) runs every tick — keeps the pipeline
#     flowing even if every LLM is dead (queue green PRs, release orphaned
#     claims, reset failed units, verify scout/intake timers, update the
#     last-heartbeat stamp, re-examine agent-blocked issues).
#   tier 2 (judgment) runs ONLY when the triage file is non-empty or the
#     held queue has dispatchable items, and walks a seat ladder
#     (claude-opus-5 -> devin glm-5-2 [after 30s probe] -> minimax M3).
#     All dead -> loud triage line + unit FAILS (systemd's failed state is
#     the page; no auto-retry, no fallback, no --collect).
#
# No polling loops inside the script; one pass per timer fire.
# fleet-ops#428: direct Telegram paging removed. A failed heartbeat falls
# through to the global unit-escalation drop-in (STOP-REASON -> senior
# auditor). Nish is only reached for Nish-reserved boundary items via
# nish-boundary-notify.

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
# Canonical live-install checkout (fleet-ops#372). products/fleet-ops is
# retargeted to this path by fleet-ops-retarget-products once no worktrees
# remain on the pre-rewrite parent (fleet-ops#410). Do not install from
# the parent. Pinning here replaces the hand-built
# fleet-heartbeat.service.d/10-deploy-checkout.conf drop-in.
Environment=FLEET_OPS_CHECKOUT=<local-path>
EnvironmentFile=-<local-path>
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
ExecStart=<local-path>
# tier 1 budget: 10 minutes (gh + jq only, fast).
# tier 2 budget: 40 minutes max (one Claude attempt is the slow one; the
#   devin probe + minimax ladder is bounded below that). Total fits inside
#   one timer interval (30 min) with a 10 min safety margin; if tier 2
#   blows past this, it is broken and must fail visibly.
TimeoutStartSec=45min
# Never restart on success OR failure: the next timer fire is the retry.
# systemd's failed state IS the signal; if we restart in here we hide it.
Restart=no

Description=Fleet LiteLLM /health/readiness canary (fleet-ops#4130 P1)
Documentation=https://github.com/Nishfleet/fleet-ops/issues/4130
# 60s timer (not the 5-min metrics-export cadence) because the proxy is a
# daemon whose death must surface in <2 min. The 60s timer is the named
# reason; the absent() rule is FleetLitellmHealthCanaryAbsent.
#
# OnFailure is wired by the global service.d/10-escalate.conf drop-in:
# a connection-refused (organ dead) exit climbs the ladder.

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
# GET /health is auth-gated (user_api_key_auth). Without this file the canary
# sees 401 and is blind, which is the fleet-ops#4628 failure. The leading
# '-' keeps CI/hosts without a live key from failing unit load.
EnvironmentFile=-<local-path>
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 <local-path>
# Starvation headroom, not a longer verdict budget (senior auditor 2026-09-11).
# 30s was the tightest start timeout of any network canary here (siblings:
# siterep-uptime 1min, fleet-deploy-check 5min, demo-brand-timeline 30min,
# search-tier 30min, sneaker-resale-recall 45min). Under the memory pressure
# that is this box's normal state, 30s is a knife: at 2026-09-11T05:06:51 IST
# this unit was SIGTERMed with result=timeout having printed NOTHING and
# written NO prom file (3.277s CPU against 0.18s for a healthy run, i.e.
# starved, not slow), so the trip carried no diagnosis and the organ
# heartbeat metric went dark for the window. Measured worst case for a
# complete run is 70s (readiness 60s + pg 5s + redis 5s, proven against a
# black-hole listener; readiness 60s = 2026-09-13, see the canary source —
# Prisma-connection stalls made /health/readiness hang 38s-6min), so 150s is
# ~2.1x headroom. Verdict latency is set by the 60s timer + the script's own
# 60s dead-tolerance (tick count), NOT by this timeout, so the extra headroom
# delays no detection and stops a starved run from being killed before it
# can report.

Restart=no

Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000

# `exec ...` keeps the inner process as PID 1's child so signals propagate.

ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path>

# fleet-seat-comeback-release.timer — periodic ACTIVE release of walled seats
# fleet-ops#2421.
#
# Runs every 15 minutes, aligned with seat-caps.json
# walled_comeback.min_probe_interval_s=900. A walled seat whose wall clock
# (bench_until ?? usable_at) has passed is re-probed with a TOOL-USING
# bash-compute probe (pi --print "Run `echo $((6*7))` via the bash tool and
# reply with the integer it prints") so a partial 503 storm that answers
# inline but 503s on tool loading stays walled (fleet-ops#2661). A
# provably-usable seat is UNWALLED (healthy observation written to the
# ledger); a failed probe re-benches the wall (fleet-ops#2493) and
# increments the seat's consecutive_failure_count. fleet-ops#2638: when
# usable_at has passed but bench_until is held by a recent re-bench the
# prober forces a real probe so the re-bench loop cannot hold a chronically-
# failing seat indefinitely; once consecutive_failure_count crosses
# SEAT_DEAD_CONSECUTIVE_THRESHOLD (default 25) the seat is CORPSED (seat_dead=true,
# wall clocks cleared) — the fleet-ops#2415/#2422 terminal convention
# seat_usable already holds. The never-probed-comeback visibility
# (fleet_seat_comeback_never_released_total, fleet-ops#2638) is exported
# per-tick. A sweep that finds expired walls and releases nothing exits 1

[Unit]
Description=Weekly Fleet Review (WFR) — blind 6-lens senior research + conference (fleet-ops#1146)
# Named reason: the 2026-08-27 "Weekly Fleet Review approved" ledger line
# mandates a weekly (Sun post-maintenance) blind 6-lens senior research +
# conference, output capped at 5 specced actions + ledger discards, self-
# scoring, ratio-governed, output = claimed work only. agent-cron-run
# already owns seat rotation and pi --print; this unit is that runner
# with a weekly slug. Restart=on-failure re-seats a transient 429
# instead of waiting until next Sunday. TimeoutStartSec=90min: a single
# run does 6 lenses + conference + filing — heavier than a delta sweep.
StartLimitIntervalSec=1h
StartLimitBurst=3

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
# fleet-ops#6252: cron jobs must never run against a deploy checkout — a run
# dirties tracked files and fleet-deploy-check blocks merge-to-live for the
# whole run (live DEPLOY-BLOCKED 2026-09-13T01:40Z). Scratch dir under
# agent-state; model discovery writes config/model-candidates.json HERE, not
# into the clone. WorkingDirectory keeps the '-' non-fatal prefix so the unit
# starts before the ExecStartPre mkdir provisions the dir on a fresh host.
Environment=WORKDIR=<local-path>
WorkingDirectory=-<local-path>
Environment=LOG_DIR=<local-path>
Environment=PROMPTS_DIR=<local-path>
Environment=PI_BIN=<local-path>
# fleet-ops#3321: model discovery pre-pass — runs last30days, fetches
# models.dev + OpenRouter, writes config/model-candidates.json. No model is
# auditioned or routed here; the list is consumed by the seat-routing layer.
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/mkdir -p <local-path>
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/python3 <local-path>
ExecStart=<local-path> weekly-fleet-review
# fleet-ops#6744: a run may exit 0 without its Phase-3 records — 2026-09-13
# filed all seven issues then the pi session ended mid-bookkeeping (cron
# output ends "Writing the conference file and all records now"); the unit
# reported SUCCESS and the stale last-ratchet.json tripped the quality-ratchet
# canary 8 days later, killing every heartbeat tick. agent-cron-run is a
# generic per-slug runner and cannot know this job's deliverables, so the
# unit asserts them: every record the prompt mandates each week must be
# fresh (<120min — TimeoutStartSec=90min bounds the run). Missing records
# fail the unit so Restart=on-failure re-seats a new attempt instead of
# letting a half-finished review read as success until the canary pages.

RestartSec=900
TimeoutStartSec=90min

unit_source.systemd/fleet-worktree-reaper.service:
[Unit]
Description=Orphan agent-worktree reaper — daily GC (fleet-ops#2227 + #2637 + #3023 + #3995)
# Named reason for this schedule (vault: "a schedule needs a named reason"):
# worktree accumulation is a monotonic growth invariant with no event signal.
# A merged claim leaves its ~440MB worktree behind silently; only a periodic
# sweep closes the gap. The reaper is fail-safe (Mode A: merged + terminal +
# clean; Mode B: ledger-terminal + HEAD-on-origin + clean — both also gate on
# no live worker), dry-run capable, and cheap, so a daily cadence is
# proportionate. Mode B (fleet-ops#2637) is the recorded-cycle-state
# extension that catches worktrees whose worker moved on after its cycle
# ended (branch changed away from claim/issue-N to main, fix/*, etc.).
# Bound (fleet-ops#3995): the reaper enforces --max-worktrees (default 450)
# and exits 3 when the post-reap count is still over the bound, so the
# unbounded growth escalates instead of leaking silently.
#
# OnFailure is wired by the global service.d/10-escalate.conf drop-in
# (unit-escalation@fleet-worktree-reaper.service), so a failed reaper
# escalates via the standard matrix. Exit 3 (bound breach) is a non-zero
# exit, so a breach trips the same OnFailure path as a crash.

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path>
# A full sweep over ~1200 worktrees + one gh pr list per repo + one
# git ls-remote per parent is ~5min wall; Mode D (fleet-ops#3023) adds
# up to --salvage-limit bank attempts (~5-15s each on a live push,
# ~2s on an archived-repo local bank). When the bound is breached the
# pre-pass raises the salvage cap to the full backlog (fleet-ops#3995),
# so a single tick can bank the whole dirty pile — 60min covers that
# worst case with headroom.
TimeoutStartSec=60min
# Never restart: the timer is the retry. A failed reaper escalates via the
# global drop-in, not via Restart=.
Restart=no

unit_source.systemd/gh-webhook-canary.service:
[Unit]
Description=GitHub push-channel synthetic canary (fleet-ops#1464)
Documentation=https://github.com/Nishfleet/fleet-ops/issues/1464

# fleet-ops#1464 pattern 2: silence must be provable. Every 5 minutes
# (RandomizedDelaySec jitter), this unit fires the canary script. The
# script POSTs a synthetic 'issues/labeled/agent-ready' payload to the
# local receiver, asserts a 200 response, and bumps the
# fleet_gh_webhook_canary_last_green_seconds Prometheus metric.
# The dead-man is the FleetGhWebhookCanaryAbsent absent() rule in
# config/fleet_rules.yml (pages the alert-repair rail when the series
# goes absent for > 15 min) plus an optional healthchecks.io
# ping-on-success (GH_WEBHOOK_HEALTHCHECKS_URL) for an external dead-man.
# That's the standard dead-man's-switch inversion: alert on missing
# success, never on present failure alone.

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=GH_WEBHOOK_CANARY_TARGET=http://127.0.0.1:8088/webhook
Environment=GH_WEBHOOK_CANARY_SECRET_FILE=%h/.config/fleet-ops/gh-webhook.secret
Environment=GH_WEBHOOK_CANARY_PROM=/var/lib/prometheus/node-exporter/fleet-gh-webhook-canary.prom
Environment=GH_WEBHOOK_CANARY_DRY=0
# healthchecks.io ping URL (external dead-man). Read from a local env
# file so the secret never lives in the repo. Optional: empty = no ping.
EnvironmentFile=-%h/.config/fleet-ops/gh-webhook-hc.env
# P14 systemd-analyze dodge: hosted runners lack <local-path> The repo
# install.sh symlinks the script to <local-path> for the live box.
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 %h/.local/bin/gh-webhook-canary
# Starvation headroom (senior auditor 2026-09-11). Same knife as
# fleet-litellm-health-canary.service: 30s is the tightest start timeout of
# any network canary here, and this unit produced the same blank trip in the
# same memory-pressure class (SIGTERM at 30s, nothing printed, no prom file
# written, so the dead-man series went dark and the trip carried no
# diagnosis). Verdict latency is set by the 5-minute timer and the
# FleetGhWebhookCanaryAbsent absent() window, NOT by this timeout.
TimeoutStartSec=120

[Unit]
Description=Headless OAuth refresh of SuperGrok xai-oauth seat (fleet-ops#41)
# Named reason for this schedule (vault: "a schedule needs a named reason"):
# SuperGrok's OAuth access token has a 6 h lifetime. A stale token in
# <local-path> makes the seat LOOK ready (pi auth check tests
# presence only) and 401 the moment a worker picks it. fleet-seat-live-
# validate (fleet-ops#917 / #1450) catches the dead case every heartbeat
# tick but does not HEAL it — this unit is the heal path. 4 h is well
# inside the 6 h access-token lifetime and matches the standard
# prepaid-quota renewal posture; Persistent=true catches up after a
# sleeping box.
#
# OnFailure is wired by the global service.d/10-escalate.conf drop-in
# (unit-escalation@grok-token-refresh.service), so a failed refresh
# joins the escalation matrix mechanically instead of burning the
# SuperGrok week silently.
#
# fleet-ops#366: this unit is the prevention mechanism for the failure
# class "stale SuperGrok credential makes the seat 401". The timer
# (grok-token-refresh.timer) is the trigger; the script is the fix.
# The live seat is xai-oauth (stnly/pi-grok, fleet-ops#1163), not the
# cap=0 legacy `grok` models.json entry.
Documentation=file:<local-path>

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path>
# The OAuth POST + jq rewrite is bounded well under a minute.
TimeoutStartSec=2min
# Never restart: the timer is the retry. A failed refresh escalates via
# the global drop-in, not via Restart= (a stuck refresh must not loop
# on a back-to-back retry).
Restart=no

Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path>
# Scan + SIGTERM + 15s grace per stale pid. 22 ccd-cli in session-33934
# that die on TERM finish well under a minute; a stuck handful still
# fits inside 15 min.
TimeoutStartSec=15min
Restart=no

unit_source.systemd/pi-intake@.timer:
[Unit]
Description=Pi fleet issue intake schedule for Nishfleet/%i

[Timer]
# fleet-ops#1464: with the GitHub push channel live (workers/github-push-
# forward/ + gh-webhook-receiver.service), the intake timer is no longer
# the primary trigger — that is webhook → receiver → pi-intake@<repo>.
# The timer is the RECONCILER: it catches what the webhook missed.
# Cadence dropped from */15 to */20 (still inside the 15-30 min envelope
# the issue names) so a healthy webhook path doesn't get its work pre-
# empted by a stale poll, and so the fleet_intake_reconciler_caught_total
# counter (in lib/pi-intake-tick.sh) rises only when the webhook path is
# genuinely degraded. A rising counter means the dead-man's switch on
# the canary + receiver should fire first.
OnCalendar=*:00/20
RandomizedDelaySec=120
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
unit_source.systemd/pi-intake@.service:
[Unit]
Description=Pi fleet issue intake tick for Nishfleet/%i
OnFailure=pi-intake-repair@%i.service
# Retry ladder is systemd's own; StartLimit* must live in [Unit].
StartLimitIntervalSec=1h
# fleet-ops#3695: worker-exit top-ups (pi-issue@.service ExecStopPost) start
# this unit up to once per debounce window (60 s). At 8/h the start limit
# tripped on a busy hour and silenced the timer tick with it.
StartLimitBurst=90

[Service]
Type=simple
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=20
RuntimeDirectory=pi-intake-%i
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
ExecCondition=/bin/sh -c 'out=$$(gh issue list -R Nishfleet/%i -l agent-ready --json number -L 1 2>&1) || { echo "gh failed: $$out" >&2; exit 255; }; [ "$$out" != "[]" ]'
# Seat rotation is pi-packet-run's documented job ("Pick a DIFFERENT seat on
# each restart"), and the retry ladder is systemd's own Restart=/RestartSec=/
# StartLimitBurst=. Nothing here is hand-rolled: ExecStartPre builds the packet,
# pi-packet-run picks the seat, systemd owns the retries.
#
# A pinned --provider minimax previously died with HTTP 429 on every repo when
# MiniMax hit its 5h rolling window (2026-08-25), stalling the whole fleet
# while healthy seats sat unused.
#
# pi-intake-run holds an exclusive flock so a manual `systemctl start` racing
# the timer is a no-op instead of a second tick (fleet-ops#26).
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c '{ cat <local-path>; echo; echo "TARGET REPO: Nishfleet/%i"; } > %t/pi-intake-%i/intake-%i.pkt'
ExecStart=<local-path> %i
TimeoutStartSec=1800

unit_source.systemd/pi-scout-repair@.service:
[Unit]
Description=Pi fleet scout repair agent for Nishfleet/%i
StartLimitIntervalSec=21600
StartLimitBurst=2

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
# Same wrapper as pi-scout@.service: pick_seat, fail loud when every seat
# is walled. Do not pin --provider here — a hardcoded repair seat is how
# this unit sat activating on quota_exhausted glm-5-2 (fleet-ops#130).
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path> %i scout-repair'
# 75 = pi-scout-run's "no usable seat" SKIP (saturated pool), same reserved
# code pi-scout@.service already carries. Without this the repair unit was
# marked FAILED for a non-fault and the unit-escalation@%n drop-in wrote a
# STOP-REASON per SKIP, which invited another retry into the same saturated
# pool (fleet-ops#5071). Only this one reserved code — real failures still
# escalate.
SuccessExitStatus=75
# fleet-ops#6577: this hop is the chain terminal. pi-scout@'s OnFailure
# summons THIS unit only after the scout's own ExecStopPost futility-end has
# run, so a provider wall that killed both hops used to end with two failed
# units, a counted wall-crash #1, and no dispatch until the next ~4h timer
# re-fire (2026-09-14T04:15Z: pi-scout@0509 + pi-scout-repair@0509 both died
# on `Connection error.` 11s apart; this template carried no ExecStopPost at
# all, so the chain-terminal exit was observed by nothing). end-repair
# classifies this unit's own journal; a terminal wall-class exit emits one
# LOUD SCOUT-WALL-CHAIN-DEAD triage line that the existing detector->queue
# reconciler files as ONE `alarm: SCOUT-WALL-CHAIN-DEAD` issue, deduped per
# wall-storm. Leading '-' so a detector fault never marks the unit further.
ExecStopPost=-/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path> end-repair %i'
TimeoutStartSec=3600

[Unit]
Description=Pi fleet product scout for Nishfleet/%i (work supply for autonomous lanes; event-driven intake exists for claiming, but generation needs periodic product inspection)
OnFailure=pi-scout-repair@%i.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
# fleet-ops#540: rest when remaining work is >= 24h at the measured drain
# rate; run when below that. A hardcoded issue count (the old `-lt 12`)
# treated 1 issue as 1 hour and blocked go-ham while a fast drain still
# had <12h of work. Missing helper is 255 so systemd does not skip-quiet.
# /bin/bash -c keeps systemd-analyze verify from needing the dest in CI.
ExecCondition=/bin/bash -c 'bin=<local-path>; if [ ! -x "$$bin" ]; then echo "work-supply-gate missing" >&2; exit 255; fi; exec "$$bin" gate %i'
# fleet-ops#454: snapshot the agent-ready buffer around the scout so a
# green run that files nothing cannot loop quietly. Leading '-' so a
# tracker fault never skips the scout or trips OnFailure repair.
ExecStartPre=-/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path> begin %i'
# Seat rotation is pi-scout-run's job (pick_seat). A pinned --provider
# previously died with HTTP 429 while healthy seats sat unused (fleet-ops#130).
# /bin/bash -c exec keeps systemd-analyze verify from needing a new CI stub
# (same shape as stop-escalation.service / unit-escalation@.service).
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path> %i scout'
# 75 = pi-scout-run's "no usable seat" SKIP (saturated pool: the claim workers
# won the seat race). Without this the unit went FAILED and OnFailure summoned
# pi-scout-repair@%i for a non-fault, which failed identically. Not a
# SuccessExitStatus fudge of real errors: only this one reserved code.
SuccessExitStatus=75
ExecStopPost=-/bin/bash -c 'exec <local-path> end %i'
# 10800s (3h): #4450 raised scout workload 5x (label_budget 8->40) but this
# budget stayed 3600 — every tick died 143/'timeout' at 1h mid-turn for 8+
# days (2026-09-13 wedge: 2x-slow lane, turns 13-22min). A 5400 bridge was
# PROVEN insufficient (run H died AT 5400s mid-turn, no PACKET-VERDICT);
# repair's numbers: 60-110min need, 8 turns = 176min. 10800 = 1.6x worst-need,
# fits the 4h OnCalendar cadence; retires the hand-placed .d bridge (#4547 class).
TimeoutStartSec=10800

[Unit]

ExecStart=<local-path>
TimeoutStartSec=900
Restart=no

[Unit]
Description=Check the nish-vault for Syncthing sync conflicts every 10 minutes (fleet-ops#529)
# Named reason: freeze-on-conflict is self-clearing only while this timer
# fires. 10 minutes is the resolver's DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_SEC window and the
# standing-rules wait ("one resolver cycle before escalating"). Persistent
# so a reboot does not leave the freeze stuck.

[Timer]
OnBootSec=3min
OnUnitActiveSec=10min
AccuracySec=30s
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=30s
Unit=vault-conflict-resolver.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
unit_source.systemd/vault-conflict-resolver.service:
[Unit]
Description=Auto-resolve Syncthing conflicts in the nish-vault (fleet-ops#529)
Documentation=file:<local-path>
# Named reason for this oneshot: any *.sync-conflict-* file freezes every
# vault writer on Mac and VPS. The 2026-08-23 control-plane wipe deleted
# the timer and the freeze sat until a human noticed on 2026-08-24. The
# unit lives in fleet-ops so deploy restores it; the heartbeat canary
# screams if it dies.
ConditionPathIsDirectory=<local-path>
# fleet-ops#1460: the .path unit (vault-conflict-resolver.path) can fire
# rapidly — a single file creation generates multiple inotify events, and
# PathExistsGlob retriggers while the conflict file exists. The default
# 5/10s burst is blown through in under a second, wedging BOTH this service
# AND the .path unit (same wedge as fleet-seat-recovery #617). The resolver
# is idempotent and exits 0 when no conflicts remain; raise the limit so a
# burst of conflict files cannot wedge the fast path. StartLimit* must live
# in [Unit], not [Service] (same convention as pi-intake@.service).
StartLimitIntervalSec=1h
StartLimitBurst=200

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=HOME=<local-path>
Environment=PATH=<local-path>
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
WorkingDirectory=<local-path>
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 <local-path>
# Exit 1 is reserved for a future "conflicts found, worker dispatched"
# signal; treat it as success so a dispatch does not trip unit-escalation.
SuccessExitStatus=0 1
TimeoutStartSec=2min
Restart=no
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=idle
NoNewPrivileges=true
StateDirectory=vault-conflict-resolver

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
unit_source.systemd/vault-conflict-resolver.path:
[Unit]
Description=Fleet vault conflict resolver — path watch for *.sync-conflict-* (replaces 10-min timer)
Documentation=file:<local-path>
# Event-driven: fires when Syncthing creates a *.sync-conflict-* file.
# The 10-min timer is kept as a dead-man backstop (silence stays loud).
# systemd PathExistsGlob does NOT support ** recursive globbing (systemd 255),
# so we watch the vault root and its top-level subdirectories. The resolver
# scans the full tree; the path unit provides the fast trigger, the timer
# backstops conflicts in deep subdirectories the path unit cannot see.
# fleet-ops#1460: the .path unit can fire rapidly — a single file creation
# generates multiple inotify events, and PathExistsGlob retriggers while the
# conflict file exists. The default 5/10s burst is blown through in under a
# second, wedging the path unit with start-limit-hit. Raise the limit so a
# burst of conflict files cannot wedge the fast path. StartLimit* must live
# in [Unit] for .path units (same convention as pi-intake@.service).
StartLimitIntervalSec=1h
StartLimitBurst=200

[Path]
PathExistsGlob=<local-path>
PathExistsGlob=<local-path> Inbox/*.sync-conflict-*
PathExistsGlob=<local-path> Knowledge/*.sync-conflict-*
PathExistsGlob=<local-path>
Unit=vault-conflict-resolver.service

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
